assumedContext: No primary filing could be retrieved: every external domain is blocked by this environment egress proxy, including sec.gov and abc.xyz. Findings rest on search-result summaries of Alphabet 8-K/10-Q releases and reputable press.
Sector recorded as software; the advertising business is priced by auction and the cloud business by contract, so Phase 1 covers both mechanisms.

findings.claim: Alphabet sets no list price in its largest business. Search advertising is priced by continuous auction, so pricing power shows up as auction density and advertiser competition rather than as a rate card.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the ads business model

findings.claim: The auction is still tightening despite AI disruption fears: Search revenue grew 17% year on year in Q2 2026 to USD 63.3bn, from about USD 54.2bn.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: On 2 September 2026 Judge Brinkema rejected all three of the DOJ structural remedies in the ad tech case, including divestiture of AdX and open-sourcing the DFP final auction logic. Google keeps the ad stack and takes behavioural remedies instead: interoperability with competitors and an end to practices that depress publisher rates.
findings.label: REGULATORY STATUTE

findings.claim: The written ad tech ruling is under seal for 14 days for redactions and the parties must file a jointly proposed Final Judgment by 2 October 2026. Google has said it will appeal the liability finding.
findings.label: REGULATORY STATUTE

findings.claim: In the search case, Judge Mehta declined the severest remedies — no Chrome divestiture, no Android breakup, no ban on distribution payments — and instead limited exclusivity and tying. Google may continue paying Apple for default placement provided no agreement runs more than one year.
findings.label: REGULATORY STATUTE

findings.claim: Both the search liability finding and its remedy are on appeal to the D.C. Circuit — Google filed notice in mid-January 2026 with its opening brief in May, and the DOJ with state attorneys general cross-appealed for stronger remedies. Briefing was still under way in late August 2026.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: Taken together, the two antitrust cases resolved at the district level without a structural break-up. The company that was widely expected to be dismantled has kept Chrome, Android, the ad stack and its distribution deals, and now faces conduct rules rather than divestiture.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived from the Mehta and Brinkema outcomes

findings.claim: Alphabet pays Apple an estimated USD 20bn a year for default search placement — a cost to Alphabet of roughly 12% of estimated FY2026 operating income, now capped at one-year terms and open to competitive bidding each year.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE
findings.source: Derived: USD 20bn against ~USD 170bn estimated FY2026 operating income; payment figure from US v. Google court documents

findings.claim: The 12-month rule cuts both ways and is arguably worse for Alphabet than for Apple. Apple can now auction the default annually; Alphabet must re-win it annually, and cannot buy exclusivity at any price.
findings.label: ANALYST ESTIMATE

findings.claim: Cloud pricing power is contractual and improving fast: Google Cloud operating margin rose from 20.7% to 35.6% year on year in Q2 2026 while revenue grew 82%. Margin expanding with volume is the signature of genuine pricing power rather than share bought with discount.
findings.label: FACT

findings.claim: The competitive threat is real but moving in Alphabet favour. ChatGPT share of the AI assistant market fell below 50% for the first time in 2026, from 87.2% two years earlier, while Gemini grew from 5.4% to over 21%; Gemini share of chatbot web traffic rose from 5.7% to 27.7%.
findings.label: CONSENSUS
findings.source: TechCrunch 2026-06-16; Similarweb via vertu; First Page Sage, 2026

findings.claim: Gemini has roughly 662 million monthly users against ChatGPT 1.1 billion and Claude 245 million. Alphabet is second in assistants while remaining first in search — the distribution advantage has not yet been broken.
findings.label: CONSENSUS

findings.claim: Dual-class share structure concentrates voting control with the founders through Class B shares. Minority holders of Class A and non-voting Class C carry the economics with limited governance recourse.
findings.label: FACT

risks.text: Both antitrust cases remain live on appeal, with the DOJ seeking stronger remedies. A D.C. Circuit reversal could reopen structural risk that the market has now largely discounted away.
The ~USD 20bn Apple distribution payment must be re-won annually and cannot be made exclusive, so the cost can rise while the protection cannot.
Dual-class control means minority holders cannot force capital discipline if the AI capex cycle disappoints.

catalysts.text: Unsealed ad tech opinion reveals the scope of behavioural remedies
Jointly proposed Final Judgment filed in the ad tech case
D.C. Circuit ruling on the search case, both appeals

conclusions: Alphabet emerged from two antitrust cases at district level with its structure intact: no Chrome divestiture, no Android breakup, no AdX divestiture, and distribution payments permitted. The break-up scenario that overhung this equity for two years did not happen.

Pricing power is demonstrated rather than asserted. Search grew 17% in Q2 2026 against a consensus expectation of AI-driven erosion, and Cloud expanded operating margin from 20.7% to 35.6% while growing 82% — margin rising with volume is the signature of real pricing power.

The same 12-month, non-exclusive rule that repriced Apple's largest profit line repriced Alphabet's largest single cost. Alphabet must now re-win the Apple default every year and cannot buy exclusivity at any price.

The competitive picture in assistants improved through 2026: ChatGPT fell below 50% share for the first time while Gemini rose above 21%, and Gemini share of chatbot web traffic went from 5.7% to 27.7%.
What remains is conduct risk, not existence risk — but both cases are live on appeal with the DOJ pressing for more, so the tail has not closed.
thesisImpact: Phase 1 removes the reason most bears held this name at a discount. The legal overhang that justified a structurally cheap multiple has largely resolved in Alphabet's favour, and the operating evidence contradicts the AI-disruption thesis on Search. That shifts the entire question to capital allocation — which is where Phases 2 and 4 find the actual risk.
